title: Test cancellation between resource creation and async context entry
applies_when: A Python async context manager creates a resource before __aenter__ returns, or a request acquires a semaphore permit before awaiting a lock and allocating its stream. Cleanup must match the ownership actually reached at each await.
lesson: A shielded __aexit__ does not cover cancellation raised inside __aenter__. Trace ownership at every await after successful creation. Reproduce with the real constructor and cleanup, synchronizing cancellation at the creation-return boundary; retain the manager so GC cannot hide delayed cleanup. Pair normal exit, cancellation, explicit cleanup and finalization controls. In AnyIO TemporaryDirectory, the second worker only called the stdlib __enter__, which returns name without I/O; returning name directly removes that gap and lets pending cancellation reach a body checkpoint followed by shielded exit. A matched regression failed on four backend variants on each native Windows/Linux CPython3.12.13 baseline and passed after the change; the tempfile module passed 84 tests per platform. For an added async lock, distinguish an acquired semaphore permit from an allocated stream: cancellation during lock entry can reach cleanup before stream_id exists, masking CancelledError with UnboundLocalError. Use a gated real request body and public concurrent requests; prove the suspension point, then compare exact baseline and proposed source. Shielding cleanup does not initialize missing state. Keep failed setup costs separate from test runtime.
avoid_when: Do not delete arbitrary entry awaits or bypass an __enter__ with side effects, validation or a different return value. A necessary await after acquisition needs explicit failure cleanup or a justified shielding strategy. Retained resource lifetime is not permanent leakage if explicit cleanup/finalization still works. Respect intentional non-deletion modes. The HTTPcore reproduction establishes cancellation masking, not exhausted semaphore capacity, overall thread safety, Trio behavior or performance. Do not fix it by skipping all post-allocation cleanup or automatically removing synchronization. These scoped tests omit optional Blockbuster instrumentation and full cross-version CI. The linked PRs are proposed, not merged, and do not establish a general Scout utility or performance gain.

evidence.note: Language-level expansion awaits __aenter__ before entering the try/finally that invokes __aexit__; entry failure is a separate ownership boundary.
Pinned stdlib TemporaryDirectory.__enter__ returns name; __exit__, cleanup and finalization have distinct deletion behavior. Do not generalize this shortcut to other managers.
Public minimal acquisition regression and direct-name fix, with independently reported Windows/Linux baseline failures and candidate tests. Explicit cleanup cancellation is separate work in PR1316.

Standalone real TCP HTTP/2 public-pool probe: Windows CPython3.12.13/3.14.3 base10a6582 propagates CancelledError, proposed aaf674a masks it with UnboundLocalError before stream allocation. Same-connection warmup/resumed-upload/subsequent-request controls pass. Independent review of another author's open PR, not a new or accepted fix.
